articles.title: Charcuterie boards are a hosting must-have — experts share how to create the best spread
articles.summary: Chefs and hosting experts share the best boards you need to build a charcuterie spread and their recommendations for the best meats and cheeses to include.
articles.body: Charcuterie boards can make any occasion feel fancy and festive, be it a casual book club meeting or a large wedding. Plus, with hundreds of cheeses, meats and garnishes to choose from, you can get as creative as you want. But whether you’re hosting a massive guest list or a small group of friends, building the perfect charcuterie board takes practice. To help you create a delicious and beautiful spread, I asked chefs and caterers about everything to keep in mind. I also gathered boards and accessories that my experts and NBC Selected editors recommend. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Best charcuterie and cheese boards of 2026 Best overall board When I first came across this gorgeous marble board, I immediately added it to my wedding registry. Three years later, it’s one of my favorite functional yet display-worthy items in my house. The board is adorned with an etched honeycomb pattern and small gold-finished honeybees. You can separately purchase a set of three stainless steel, brass-finished cheese knives in a matching design, including a pronged knife for hard cheeses, an oval knife for soft cheeses and a wide-blade knife for semi-hard cheeses. There’s also a round version that includes the cheese knives. Best pre-made charcuterie board For the past few years, my family gifts me Boarderie charcuterie boards for birthdays and anniversaries (and, most recently, I received one for my apartment move). The boards are pre-assembled and ready-to-eat, with artisan cheeses, meats and pairings like crackers, dried fruits, nuts and chocolates. Best of all, it gets shipped directly to my door, so I don’t have to worry about doing any of the work. Boarderie is also a favorite of NBC Selected commerce editor Bethany Heitman: “I’m always looking for ways to make entertaining easier, and the ready-made charcuterie boards from Boarderie are one of my best secret weapons,” she says. “They ship quickly and arrive fully arranged, so you can just open the box and set it out, which makes them a great way to feed a crowd with minimal effort.” Each of Boarderie’s cheese and charcuterie boards is available in three sizes that serve up to 14 people. This year, Boarderie launched dessert charcuterie boards filled with sweet treats, which makes it even more giftable. Best personalizable You can personalize this board with an engraved monogram, which makes it stylish and classy for events, says Emmy Rener, founder of cheese and charcuterie shop Sophisticated Spreads. Made from a combination of wood and marble, this serving platter comes with three small condiment bowls for your extras and spreadables, like jams, honey, olives and more. The brand recommends wiping the platter clean with a damp cloth, and warns that the marble is naturally porous, so it might stain from extensive contact with oily or colorful foods. Best for large spreads Best serving platter This circular serving platter is an elegant and attractive base to assemble your charcuterie spread on, according to Sarah Simms, co-founder of cheese and charcuterie shop Lady & Larder. It’s microwave- and dishwasher-safe, and comes in white and aqua. Most compact This round board folds into itself for easy storage, but expands to make room for all of your favorite treats. It has four tiers, so you can designate a specific food to each one if you prefer they don’t touch. It also has a slide-out drawer equipped with cheese knives. I have the 13-inch size of this board and love taking it when I have a small gathering with friends. The smaller size comes with two cheese knives (an all-purpose, stainless steel cheese knife and a cheese fork), and the larger size (17-inch diameter) includes an additional flat cheese knife. Best for small spreads If you want something small and simple, consider this Mark & Graham marble board, which is a favorite of Rener’s due to its whimsical scalloped design. If you’re stuck on a unique gift idea, you can also customize it with a monogram. Keep in mind, the brand recommends hand washing it only. Best multipurpose Although this is a traditional cutting board set, each one also serves as a great charcuterie tray, says NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin. It includes boards in three sizes, so you can choose one that makes the most sense for your spread. “You can also make up to three charcuterie boards at once — for example, sometimes I do one with meat, one vegetarian and a nut-free one, depending on who I’m serving,” says Malin. The boards also have indents to keep food that tends to roll away (like olives or chocolate-covered almonds) in place. Plus, they’re easy to clean: Malin washes them with warm water and dish soap, and they dry quickly. Best for beginners If you’re a charcuterie beginner, the visual map on this one indicates where to place cheeses, meats, fruits and more. The board, which comes recommended by Rener, also has a handle so you can take it on the go. Most giftable If you’re a music lover, consider this unique board with a turntable-inspired design. It comes with a removable slate platter designed to look like a record, as well as a wooden outer base to hold the platter. Lift up the record player “needle” and you’ll find a hidden cheese slicer too. Most sleek Marble helps food stay cold, so this board is great for keeping meats and cheeses fresh, says Malin. The board also doesn’t tend to absorb odors or colors, so she can serve colorful fruits or veggies (like beets) without worrying about stains, she says. Plus, it sits on non-slip rubber feet, which allows Malin to easily lift and move it. “I think the elevation is a nice way to showcase a beautiful board you created,” she adds. How I picked the best charcuterie boards and accessories When shopping for a charcuterie board, the experts I spoke to recommend keeping the following factors in mind: Type of spread: Your charcuterie spread — meaning the different foods you’ll be presenting — directly impacts the type of board and tools you’ll need. Consider whether your focus is strictly meats or cheeses, or if you’re adding spreadables like jams or honey, fruits, nuts and other extras that’ll require more room (and more flavor and texture considerations).Board type: You can use virtually any kind of board for your charcuterie spread, including cheese boards, plastic trays and cutting boards. I included a variety of options on this list.Board size and food amount: The size of your board depends on how much food you’re preparing and how many guests you’re feeding. You should have a minimum of two to three ounces of meat and cheese per person for an appetizer, and double that amount if it’s the main course, says Simms.Material: Most charcuterie boards are made of wood or marble, each of which has its own unique benefits. A wooden board is a favorite among my experts because it’s sturdy, durable and often comes with side ridges, dips and handles to add space and avoid spillage. Marble boards can keep cheeses and meats at a colder temperature and often look more aesthetically pleasing, experts say. A step-by-step guide to assembling your charcuterie board One of the most important considerations when crafting a charcuterie board is how to arrange the foods. Below is a step-by-step guide for the perfect meat and cheese assembly. Consider what foods you’ll be using. There are several delicious food combinations you can make on a charcuterie board. One thing remains consistent among my experts: it’s the perfect time to work with flavors you love and get creative with other tastes and textures. “When you have something out of the ordinary [on your board], that’s when it becomes a conversation piece. Charcuterie boards actually have a lot of ways of getting people connected,” says Serge Krikorian, owner and head chef of Vibrant Occasions Catering.Prioritize quality over quantity. “If you take the time to source intentionally, your board will always be delicious,” says Simms, who recommends checking out your local farmers market to find out what is in season near you.Select a good quality serving board. Choose the right sized board to fit all of your foods without them overflowing, and consider ones with indented edges to catch any loose bites or leftover juices. Some boards might also have specific dips for ramekins or handles so you can take them on the go, experts say.Determine your arrangement. A basic stack of meats and cheeses won’t be aesthetically pleasing — they need to be assembled the right way. For meats, a salami river and prosciutto ribbons are some of the prettiest and easiest ways to make meat look good, allowing them to flow across or around your board, says Rener. Don’t be afraid to work with different colors and textures, too: red grapes, for example, can make a board look more elevated compared to green grapes, and adding a darker berry, like blackberries, on top can add more height, texture and a contrasting color, according to Rener.Add bowls and other decorations. To hold loose foods like nuts and olives, consider a ramekin or small bowls for extra flair. Mini dishes are also great for jams and spreads, which not only makes them look good, but keeps them from touching other foods on the board. Meet our charcuterie experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Sarah Simms is the co-founder of cheese and charcuterie shop Lady & Larder in Los Angeles.Emmy Rener is the founder of cheese and charcuterie shop Sophisticated Spreads.Serge Krikorian is the owner and head chef of Vibrant Occasions Catering in Arkansas.Cheyenne Nichols is a chef and owner of catering company Finest Cravings. For this article, I interviewed four chefs and hosting experts about what they consider when building a charcuterie board, and compiled their favorite boards to shop. articles.title: In 2021, a Minnesota couple bought a deteriorating 1909 chapel for $115,000 and spent about $400,000 converting it into an Airbnb; it generated roughly $40,000 a year in gross revenue
articles.summary: Discover the journey of O'Mara and Adam Dunnigan as they buy and renovate a historic 1909 chapel in Minnesota, turning it into a successful Airbnb and event space. Learn about the costs, renovations, and income they generated from this unique investment.
articles.body: Small churches that once served as the centre of entire towns are becoming less active across the American Midwest. According to Lifeway Research, approximately 3,000 new Protestant churches were founded and 4,500 closed in the US in 2019. Many of those structures later serve as residences, studios or vacation rentals, but the entire cost of such a project is rarely disclosed. Compared to most, a church in northwest Minnesota provides a crisper picture.In 2021, O'Mara and Adam Dunnigan purchased a deteriorating chapel built in 1909 in Detroit Lakes for $115,000. They spent roughly a year and $400,000 converting it into an Airbnb and event space. In July 2024, O'Mara told Business Insider that the property generated about $40,000 in annual gross revenue, and the couple had listed it for $549,900. By April 2025, the asking price had dropped to $499,000, according to Valley News Live. These figures provide a picture of the purchase, renovation and reported income, but they do not establish the property's overall profitability.A chapel on the hillBy chance, or more by golf, the pair found it. While playing a round in Detroit Lakes in the summer of 2021, they noticed a small white chapel with a golden steeple on a tract of around 2.5 acres. The town is closer to Fargo, N.D., than it is to Minneapolis, and O’Mara said its population typically triples when the weather is warm, which made the concept of a rental a bit easier to believe. She’s in residential real estate, and Adam is an engineering director, so neither was starting from scratch.The peeling paint on the structure had a long history behind it. Fox 9 reports it was consecrated in June 1909 for the Saron Norwegian Lutheran congregation, while Valley News Live says services ended in 1960. The chapel was moved to its present home in 2000 and was a store and a location for events before the Dunnigans came. It was listed at $115,000 and was 3,061 sq. ft. Business Insider noticed that Zillow had the average property value in Detroit Lakes at $373,252; thus, the sticker price looked like a deal.Where the money wentTwo contractors took one look at the chapel and walked away. A local builder whose father had made church altars agreed to take it on. The work covered new support beams, insulation, a septic system, heating and cooling, plumbing and electrics, and the couple chose to keep several original features rather than strip them out. Valley News Live reported that insulation alone costs $26,000 and the septic system another $15,000. O’Mara said the 65-foot steeple was the hardest part to restore. Add the renovation figure to the purchase price and the total comes to roughly $515,000. That sum says nothing of the time two working parents gave to the project. The result was a three-bedroom home with two and a half bathrooms that doubles as a rental and a venue.What it earnedThe property operated throughout the year, with guests paying roughly $250 a night, according to O'Mara. Guests used it for graduations, birthdays, anniversaries, weddings and baby showers. In June 2024, the Dunnigans also renewed their wedding vows there after 15 years of marriage. O'Mara estimated annual gross revenue at about $40,000. That figure represents income before cleaning, utilities, insurance, taxes, maintenance and other operating expenses are deducted, so it should not be treated as profit.The couple later decided to sell because their work schedules were demanding and they wanted to focus on a vacation property they had purchased in Portugal. Business Insider reported an initial asking price of $549,900 in July 2024. By April 2025, Valley News Live reported that the price had been reduced to $499,000. These were asking prices, not confirmed sale proceeds, and they do not establish whether the couple recovered the purchase and renovation costs.The project illustrates why the purchase price alone does not reveal the cost of converting an old building into a rental property. The chapel cost $115,000, and the reported renovation spending brought the combined amount to about $515,000 before other expenses. The estimated $40,000 in annual gross revenue does not account for operating costs, and the property's asking price does not prove what a buyer would ultimately pay. The case offers a useful look at the financial demands of converting an unusual historic building, but the available figures are not enough to determine the couple's overall profit or loss.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Speaking at the third Russia-Africa Summit, Putin frames Moscow as an alternative to former colonial powers.
articles.body:
President Vladimir Putin has told African leaders visiting Moscow that Russia does not engage in “neo-colonial exploitation” of the continent, unlike former colonial powers.

Speaking at the third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow on Wednesday, Putin said the West is still trying ‌to exploit the continent’s resources and uses debt to hold back development.

“Africa is increasingly asserting itself as one of the key players in the global economy and politics. However, the emergence of a multipolar world is, of course, no easy task; it faces resistance from countries that are not prepared to accept this reality,” Putin told the summit.

Russian-backed government forces in a broad swath of North Africa are fighting armed rebellions as many countries in the region emerge from military coups that have shaken regional security.

Putin criticised “active attempts by Western countries” to drive Africans back into debt and to force them to accept much-needed financial resources on predatory terms, which he said slowed their long-term development.

“Our business does not engage in the predatory, neo-colonial exploitation of natural and human resources, but rather expands the processing of raw materials locally, thereby creating new jobs and generating tax revenue,” said Putin.

Putin told delegations from 48 African countries, including 22 represented by their heads of state, that Russia was prepared to expand the geographical reach of agricultural product shipments.

Russia had supplied 13 million metric tonnes of agricultural products to Africa in the first nine months of this year alone, he added.

The remarks come as attacks in the Black Sea continue to disrupt exports of grain from both Russia and Ukraine , while the United States-Israel war on Iran has interrupted global fertiliser supplies.

Putin is due to hold one-on-one talks with individual African leaders who are attending on topics ranging from trade to security, grain supplies and arms deals.

The summit is expected to end with a final declaration on deepening cooperation between Russia and African nations.

articles.title: Netanyahu’s fortunes improve but without clear path to outright victory
articles.summary: JERUSALEM — Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s fortunes changed Wednesday as vote counting in Israel wound down, with his Likud party and coalition partners edging out the leading competitor, retired Gen. Gadi Eisenkot. Netanyahu’s Likud party was projected to hold 26 seats in Israel’s parliament, the Knesset, with more than 80 percent of the votes…
articles.body:
JERUSALEM — Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s fortunes changed Wednesday as vote counting in Israel wound down, with his Likud party and coalition partners edging out the leading competitor, retired Gen. Gadi Eisenkot.

Netanyahu’s Likud party was projected to hold 26 seats in Israel’s parliament, the Knesset, with more than 80 percent of the votes counted by Wednesday afternoon. That was an increase from the tallies at the initial close of polls. Eisenkot’s Yashar party is projected at 21 seats, so far.

Being at the head of the largest party in the Knesset does have political power, but Netanyahu does not have a pathway to the 61 seats needed for a governing coalition without peeling off one of Eisenkot’s likely partners. Some analysts are raising the possibility of a unity government between Netanyahu and Eisenkot.

“What will be the other way? A second election,” said Udi Tenne, strategic adviser, political analyst and campaign strategist who has worked on Israeli campaigns across the ideological spectrum.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog — who is tasked with consulting the party heads, choosing who he thinks can form a government or pushing for unity — said Wednesday that another round of elections must be avoided and urged lawmakers meeting with him to have an “open mind.”

“We must do everything we can, certainly after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections,” he said during a gathering at the president’s house in Jerusalem, The Times of Israel reported .

Herzog said he expects to receive the official election results next week, and then will begin consultations.

Tenne said Netanyahu would likely achieve a more decisive victory in a second election, building on the momentum that his Likud party came out with the largest number of votes. Voters who cast their ballots for smaller, right-wing, conservative parties that failed to cross the electoral threshold would likely turn their vote to Netanyahu.

“It’s very important to understand, the biggest party is the Likud party,” Tenne said.

But Israeli Jews might prefer a repeat election, according to polling by the Israel Democracy Institute (IDI). More than a third of respondents preferred redoing the polls in the event of a stalemate. The second most preferred option was a unity government, rotating the prime minister.

A majority of Israelis also supported appointing as prime minister the head of the party with the most votes, 61 percent, according to the IDI poll, if it means increasing the stability of the political system in Israel.

But Eisenkot is not signaling, yet, that he’s looking to partner with Netanyahu.

He and his supporters have seized on the initial election results as the public rejecting Netanyahu’s leadership. Netanyahu’s bloc has achieved about 54 seats, less than his current governing coalition of 68.

“The preliminary poll results point to complete distrust in Netanyahu and the government of October 7, of the Zionist majority and of the majority of Israeli citizens,” Eisenkot posted Tuesday evening on social platform X, as his bloc showed a slight lead over Netanyahu.

For Israeli Jews and Arabs, a minority government is a poor option. A minority government rules when a coalition has less than 61 seats and counts on a bloc of lawmakers to reach a majority in favor of legislation proposals, or at least abstain and not kill a bill vote.

There’s a variety of coalition formulations Netanyahu and Eisenkot can, separately, attempt to secure the 61-seat majority.

The strong showing of Israel’s Arab political parties, Ra’am and the Joint List, could lead Eisenkot to reverse his pledge not to partner with the Arab coalition.

The two parties together are projected to have 19 seats.

It’s an impressive display of the increased voter participation among Israel’s Arab population, which represents 21 percent of the country. It was largely driven by revulsion against Itamar Ben-Gvir, the national security minister in Netanyahu’s current government.

“I think that Ben-Gvir will go out of the government this time; he’s a racist; he wants to kill as many Arabs as possible,” said a young Muslim woman from the majority Arab village of Abu Ghosh after voting Tuesday. She declined to share her name.

“Bibi also, he killed people in Gaza, and here,” she said, using a nickname for Netanyahu. “Outside of that I don’t mind to vote for anyone else, Jewish, Muslim — what’s important is that it’s not Ben-Gvir and not Netanyahu.”

Netanyahu on Wednesday accused Arab parties of stealing votes in a post on X .

“The elections in the State of Israel were stolen by Arab parties that support terrorism and the elimination of the Jewish state through serious criminal offenses of bribery, threats, violence, forgeries, and the use of prohibited software to mobilize voters,” he wrote.

The Washington Post reported that Netanyahu’s camp is lobbying President Trump to advocate for a unity government and has leveraged excluding Ben-Gvir from that ruling coalition.

It’s in Trump’s interest to see the quick formation of a stable Israeli government and begin addressing, in earnest, his goals to remake the Middle East: Eliminate the threat from Iran; move forward peace processes in Gaza, and between Israel, Lebanon and Syria; and expand the Abraham Accords, likely with Saudi Arabia.

Ben-Gvir is viewed as an obstacle to realizing those goals. An ultra-nationalist and Jewish extremist, he wants to force out Palestinians from the West Bank and the Gaza Strip and establish Israeli sovereignty over the territory.

As national security minister, he’s refused to address rising violence by extremist Israeli settlers in the West Bank. That violence is condemned by Democrats, U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee and Israel’s Muslim and Arab neighbors , including members of the Abraham Accords and from countries Trump hopes to join that normalization agreement with Israel.

Excluding Ben-Gvir from a new government is viewed as key for action to take place against this group.

“If Ben-Gvir is not there, I think you’ll see a more forceful hand against them,” said Herb Keinon, senior contributing editor and analyst at The Jerusalem Post.

Trump is maintaining public support for Netanyahu. He endorsed the prime minister ahead of the election and on Wednesday shared a quote on his social media site crediting himself with preventing Netanyahu’s defeat. The message was clear, even if whom Trump was quoting was not.

Trump “only wants what is good for the Middle East, Israel and the United States of America!” the quote read.

Kelly is in Israel participating in a media trip organized by the Israel Press Club, a nonpartisan, nongovernmental organization. The Israel Press Club facilitated some interviews and paid for flights, hotels and meals.

articles.title: Florida Senate nominee Angie Nixon says 'I don't know' when asked if she's capitalist or socialist
articles.summary: Angie Nixon repeatedly said "I don't know" when asked if she's a capitalist or socialist during a Politico "Conversation" interview Friday.
articles.body: Florida Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon struggled to identify whether she was a capitalist or socialist during an interview Friday, drawing sharp criticism from Republican Sen. Ashley Moody's campaign as the candidates entered the final week of Florida's Senate race. Politico's Dasha Burns confronted the nominee over her membership in the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), noting that she had previously identified herself as a capitalist despite joining the socialist organization. When Burns pressed Nixon to explain how she personally identified, the Jacksonville Democrat repeatedly expressed uncertainty. "I don't know. I don't know. Like, I don't know," Nixon said on "The Conversation." "I identify as Angie Nixon, as a Black woman who was a former single mom, who wants to make sure that no one has to struggle the way I struggled when I was a single mom." LA MAYORAL HOPEFUL NITHYA RAMAN CALLS HERSELF BOTH A 'CAPITALIST' AND 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST' Cameron Gambini, a spokesperson for Moody, criticized Nixon's response in a statement to Fox News Digital, questioning her ideological commitments and referencing a separate controversy surrounding her recent comments about Cuba. "Angie Nixon voluntarily signed up to be a member of the Democrat Socialists," he said. "Now, she's clearly regretting letting her true colors shine. And just yesterday, she refused to say Cuba was a dictatorship. Socialist Angie is a radical lunatic who will never step foot on the Senate floor. Case closed." When asked directly during an interview Monday with CBS News whether Nixon considered Cuba a dictatorship, she said, "You know, that is what people have told me. I have never been to Cuba, and so I will have to take their word for it." Nixon subsequently challenged CBS News' characterization of her answer, maintaining that she believed Cubans who described their government as a dictatorship. CBS deleted its initial social media post and acknowledged that its description had inaccurately represented her response. "It’s disappointing to have to say this, but [CBS News], this is a serious failure of editorial reporting," Nixon said in a post on X. "I clearly state in this clip that while I have not personally been to Cuba, I have spoken with Cubans who have described it as a dictatorship, and I believe them. To claim I declined to answer the question is categorically false. "That is not journalism. It is misinformation." Turning Point USA spokesman Andrew Kolvet criticized the Democratic nominee's response to Politico about whether she was a socialist in a statement to Fox News Digital, suggesting she was attempting to distance herself from socialism because of its political implications in Florida. "Some pollster or political consultant probably told her socialism doesn’t sell in Florida," he said. "So, she’s offering the flimsiest and most insincere of explanations for how radical and economically illiterate she really and truly is. She seems to contend that existing within the land border of America makes you a capitalist. "But just like existing in America doesn’t make someone an American, running for Senate doesn’t suddenly make Angie Nixon a good liar." WHO IS ANGIE NIXON? BULLHORN-WIELDING SOCIALIST UPSETS ESTABLISHMENT FAVORITE IN SUNSHINE STATE STUNNER Initially, in the same exchange on "The Conversation," Burns asked Nixon whether she considered herself a capitalist or socialist, prompting the Democratic nominee to first emphasize her support for government assistance programs. "So, what I would say is, I live in a capitalistic society, and I just want to make sure that people have strong social programs and safety net programs because I've had to use them before," Nixon said. "So, you can call me whatever you want, but just know that I'm going to be out here working and fighting for hardworking and retired people and folks living with disabilities." Throughout the interview, Nixon pushed back against political ideological branding, saying that she didn’t "care about labels" and considered herself a "humanist." She also said she remains a "lifelong Democrat" and noted that both she and her husband are small business owners who wouldn’t "want to take over anyone’s business." Nixon also explained that she joined the DSA due to local community work, noting how members helped her nonprofit when "the government shutdown happened" and people lost SNAP benefits. DSA CO-CHAIR MOCKED FOR PROUDLY CONFIRMING SOCIALISTS WANT TO ABOLISH THE SENATE, NATIONAL BORDERS, PRISONS Nixon's uncertainty contrasted with her August appearance on NBC News' "Meet the Press" when host Kristen Welker pressed her about her DSA membership. During the interview, Nixon rejected the socialist label and explicitly embraced capitalism. "I'm a capitalist who believes that we need some strong regulation," Nixon said. Nixon joined the DSA in June but previously rejected several proposals in its national political program, including abolishing the U.S. Senate, drafting a new Constitution and defunding the military. The organization has also advocated public ownership of major corporations and essential industries, although it did not nationally endorse Nixon's campaign. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Nixon is challenging Moody, whom Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed to the U.S. Senate after Marco Rubio became secretary of state. Fox News Digital reached out to Nixon, CBS and the DSA for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

articles.title: Netanyahu’s party alleges ‘serious criminal offenses’ in Israeli election
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party on Wednesday accused Arab political parties of stealing the country’s election through widespread voter fraud, as preliminary results showed no clear winner. In a statement shared by Netanyahu on the social platform X, Likud alleged that Arab parties engaged in bribery, voter intimidation and forgery to influence election…
articles.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party on Wednesday accused Arab political parties of stealing the country’s election through widespread voter fraud, as preliminary results showed no clear winner.

In a statement shared by Netanyahu on the social platform X, Likud alleged that Arab parties engaged in bribery, voter intimidation and forgery to influence election results, as neither Netanyahu nor his primary challenger Gadi Eisenkot was projected to gain a parliamentary majority.

“The elections in the State of Israel were stolen by Arab parties that support terrorism and the elimination of the Jewish state through serious criminal offenses of bribery, threats, violence, forgeries, and the use of prohibited software to mobilize voters,” Likud said.

The party said it was turning over hundreds of witness accounts and pieces of evidence to the Israeli police, the Shin Bet domestic security agency and the Central Elections Committee.

Likud alleges that thousands of envelopes containing cash and ballots for Ra’am, an Arab political party, were distributed to voters. The party also claimed that voters cast multiple ballots, used false identities and employed prohibited software to boost turnout.

The allegations have not been independently verified, and Likud did not publicly release the evidence it said it had collected.

“We demand from the police and the Shin Bet a thorough investigation into the election theft by the Arab parties and the full prosecution of the criminals,” the party said.

The accusations come as Netanyahu, who was endorsed by President Trump, faces an uncertain political future following an election in which an opposition bloc led by Eisenkot made historic gains and could play a decisive role in determining Israel’s next government.

With 85.6 percent of ballots counted by election authorities as of Wednesday, there is no clear winner, as Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition has won 53 seats, the opposition coalition has won 48 seats and the Arab parties have won 19 seats, with each bloc falling short of the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority.

articles.title: Who is Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu’s opponent?
articles.summary: Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot is looking to be Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s primary opponent in an election cycle where Israelis are growing displeased with current leadership. Eisenkot worked in the Israeli military for 41 years before eventually serving as the country’s military chief. He has hammered Netanyahu for security failures, calling him an “anti-leader,”…
articles.body:
Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot is looking to be Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s primary opponent in an election cycle where Israelis are growing displeased with current leadership.

Eisenkot worked in the Israeli military for 41 years before eventually serving as the country’s military chief. He has hammered Netanyahu for security failures, calling him an “anti-leader,” according to The Times of Israel .

“If, God forbid, the current right-wing coalition wins again, it will lead Israel in dark directions that we can already see unfolding,” he told The Times of Israel.

The former Israeli military chief pointed to the attempted hijacking of a Flydubai flight as a “massive security failure,” stating Netanyahu “shamelessly leverages it for a photo op.”

“This election,” Eisenkot expressed, “is a choice between responsibility and running away from responsibility.”

This race marks the first election since the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks which killed around 1,200 people. Its aftermath has become a major issue that Netanyahu has been criticized for, along with his leadership during the Iran war.

Eisenkot has campaigned on forming a “formal state commission of inquiry” about the attack. Netanyahu has reportedly blocked inquiry attempts, according to Anadolu , which cited former Israeli intelligence officer Barak Seri.

Seri accused Netanyahu of being warned about the Hamas attack before it happened but “ignored it all.”

After the Oct. 7 attack, Eisenkot joined Netanyahu’s emergency war cabinet but left in 2024 , writing, “Outside considerations and politics infiltrated into the discussions.”

Eisenkot’s campaign has also been defined by his son who died fighting in Gaza. His two nephews who were deployed to combat were also killed fighting in Gaza.

It gave him credibility, The Associated Press reported, as voters saw his personal ties to the conflict as a defining part of his potential military strategy.

Both candidates do not support the creation of a Palestinian state, though Eisenkot has expressed he would halt Israeli annexation efforts of the West Bank.

“Anyone who wants to impose full sovereignty over all of Judea and Samaria [the West Bank] and bring another 2.8 million Palestinians into Israel is endangering the Zionist enterprise and the Jewish demographic majority,” he said, per The Times of Israel.

Eisenkot would make history in Israel as the country’s first Mizrahi Jew to become prime minister. Mizrahi — Jewish people descended from the Middle East or North Africa — is estimated to be the largest Jewish ethnic group in Israel, according to researchers from Tel Aviv University and Columbia University.

To win, Eisenkot still needs to assemble a coalition of at least 61 members of the Knesset, Israel’s 120-member legislature. If he and other candidates fail, as is currently predicted by polling, Israeli President Isaac Herzog can pass the mandate to another lawmaker to try to fulfill within 28 days. If this is also not successful, the country will hold another election.

articles.title: Stanford professors Sebastian Thrun and Peter Norvig opened their artificial intelligence course to the world for free in 2011; 160,000 students from 190 countries enrolled
articles.summary: Discover how Stanford's groundbreaking artificial intelligence course opened its doors to 160,000 students worldwide, revolutionizing online education in 2011.
articles.body: In October 2011, professors from Stanford University made their introduction to Artificial Intelligence as a free course and open to anyone with internet access. Taught jointly by Stanford research professor Sebastian Thrun and Google research director Peter Norvig, who expected few sign-ups, the course exceeded their expectations when 160,000 enrolments came from more than 190 countries. According to Stanford Engineering, the course started on 10 October and ran until 18 December, forming part of a wider experiment that involved three online computer science courses offered by the university. Along with the artificial intelligence course, students enrolled in Introduction to Databases, which was taught by Jennifer Widom, and Machine Learning under Andrew Ng.A university course with assignments, tests, and international participationUnlike a typical online setting where students can learn through online lectures, the classes were structured like a course of study. According to Stanford Engineering, the course was designed to offer students more than the scope of university lectures, wherein they could work through recorded mini-lectures, complete exercises, and take examinationsIntended to run for ten weeks, the syllabus covered the tenets of artificial intelligence through models of robotics, autonomous vehicles, and software that recommends music. Students were able to go through each week’s lessons at their own pace because the teaching materials were released weekly, while mid-term and final examinations were automatically assessed. To make the video lectures more interactive, quizzes were incorporated into the system. For students wanting to test their practical skills, programming exercises were in place to assess their knowledge. However, it would be remiss not to mention that those who completed the course requirements were awarded a statement of accomplishment, but participation did not confer Stanford University academic credit.Moreover, the design of the assessments was made in a way that allowed for repeated attempts. The one responsible for this interface was Stanford computer science professor emeritus, Jeffrey Ullman. Ullman had conceptualised a testing method that relied on a pool of possible answers rather than just the visible options on a single question. As a result, the system generated different question sets for each iterative attempt a student made on a given assessment.Furthermore, the system allowed an online discussion forum, much like the setting of a classroom where the floor is opened for questions. There, students could pose questions, answer the lingering doubts of their colleagues, and vote answers up or down based on their satisfaction. Jennifer Widom, who taught the databases course, reported that this was instrumental for teachers since they couldn’t cater to all the students at once; she said, "I can see that students are answering each other's questions and that answers from the top students are going to bubble up."International participation and the implications for higher education The impact of this artificial intelligence course was felt beyond the figures it had registered; Stanford Engineering reported that students had accessed the course database more than 7,500 times per second. About 40% of the total registrants across the three courses were from the United States, and India accounted for the second-largest group.Participation wasn't just limited to the formal teaching platform, as volunteers lent a helping hand and translated the artificial intelligence course into more than 40 languages, while local study groups were formed in different places to discuss the material in person. For instructors and teachers alike, the experiment provided an opportunity to understand how students learn and thereby improve their teaching methods. With tens of thousands of participants exposed to different testing arrangements, this exercise would have been otherwise difficult to conduct with a conventional class of 50 or 60 students.Ultimately, the course’s significance lies in establishing artificial intelligence as a barrier breaker and strengthening the groundwork of teaching methodology. Up until this initiative, institutions would publish lecture recordings for remote audiences. The Stanford experiment showed the possibility of combining video instruction with structured coursework and assessment on a much larger scale.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Netanyahu is the ultimate survivor. But can he survive this time?
articles.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu hasn’t won in Israel’s elections. But he hasn’t lost, either —  at least not yet. Now, he has to stop his rivals from building their own government.
articles.body: In a political career that has spanned more than three decades, Benjamin Netanyahu has been written off too many times to count, only to prove the obituaries were penned prematurely. Israel’s election results this week appear to give the prime minister’s opponents a chance to end his run, but in the country’s ruthless political system, it’s no guarantee. By Wednesday night, most votes had been counted. But there is no clear winner for Israel’s top post, setting up weeks — possibly months — in which Netanyahu’s political survival remains on the line. With the vote counting nearing its conclusion, Netanyahu’s Likud party remains the largest party in the 120-seat parliament, known as the Knesset, with an estimated 26 seats. But his right-wing bloc has lost its majority, set to win only 53 seats, short of the 61-seat majority needed to govern. Netanyahu hasn’t won. But he hasn’t lost, either — at least not yet. Now, he has to stop his rivals from building their own government, and he may survive again. The Arab parties On paper, the opposition holds roughly 67 seats, but that arithmetic is fractured by ideological, national and personal rivalries. Netanyahu’s main challenger, Gadi Eisenkot, won 21 seats, but the Jewish opposition parties total only 48, well short of victory. To reach 61, they would need the support of two Arab parties, Raam and the Joint List, which are projected to win a record 19 seats between them. Analysts say that record turnout by Arabs or Palestinian citizens of Israel was in part a backlash to four years of a far-right national security minister under whom crime in the Arab community soared. This is where the math gets complicated. Raam is an Islamist party that draws heavily from Israel’s Bedouin community. Its leader, Mansour Abbas, became the first Arab politician to join an Israeli government following the country’s 2021 election. The Joint List, projected to be the bigger Arab party, combines several smaller parties: the Communist Hadash, secularist Taal and nationalist Balad factions. On Wednesday, Yair Golan, leader of the left-wing Democrats party, called on his partners to count the Arab parties as part of the bloc, rejecting what he called Netanyahu’s “racist division between Jewish and Arab votes.” But two of Eisenkot’s right-wing allies, Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Liberman, have opposed any government that depends on the Arab parties. (They have not issued a statement on the issue since polls closed.) The Joint List said Wednesday that it was ready for political cooperation and willing to do “do everything in its power to bring Netanyahu’s rule to an end.” What will Netanyahu do? A source close to Netanyahu said his main post-election goal is to delegitimize and therefore prevent the Jewish-Arab political cooperation that could send him home. “He is very concerned about a minority government,” the source said. Netanyahu even plans to pressure individual opposition lawmakers not to cooperate with the Arab parties. After campaigning against them throughout the election, Likud issued a statement Wednesday accusing the Arab parties of “stealing the election” through bribery, threats, violence and forgery, echoing election fraud claims from his closest ally, US President Donald Trump. The Central Elections Committee said Wednesday it was examining the complaint, but the committee had already dismissed thousands of complaints from the different parties on election day. Netanyahu plans to “neutralize this possibility by all means,” the source told CNN, “including launching an attack on Iran or enlisting President Trump to intervene in Israeli politics on his behalf.” The opposition fears that Netanyahu could use a security crisis to stall or block a new government. Before the election, Netanyahu had pressed Trump to launch a joint attack on Iran, but Washington held off, partly because Israeli military chief of staff Eyal Zamir warned it could disrupt the vote. An Israeli security source told CNN the operational plans are ready and awaiting Trump’s approval, possibly after the US midterms. “There is no way to know what Netanyahu will do,” an opposition source told CNN. “We are aware that he may try to push for another escalation.” Another source said that Netanyahu “will do everything he can not to leave the prime minister’s office, including domestic and external chaos.” Eisenkot, a former Israel Defense Forces chief of staff, called on Israel’s security chiefs Tuesday night to remember that “Netanyahu is a caretaker prime minister, without a mandate and without public confidence.” Speaking to supporters shortly after exit polls were published, Eisenkot declared that the public “has chosen change.” In his first reaction to the updated results since Tuesday night’s speech, Eisenkot said he remains committed to “bringing change to Israel.” What comes next The numbers can still change. By Wednesday evening, the Central Elections Committee is expected to finish counting most ballots. Attention now turns to double-envelope ballots from home by soldiers, prisoners, hospital patients and staff, diplomats abroad and voters with disabilities. The committee estimates there are between 430,000 and 480,000 double envelopes, enough for over 10 seats. They are counted separately in a special verification process, with final results expected Thursday. Then the political maneuvering begins in earnest. The next step runs through President Isaac Herzog, whose post-election role is pivotal. His job here is to consult with all elected parties on the candidate they recommend as prime minister, before picking the one he believes is most likely to secure a 61-seat majority. This is not necessarily the leader of the largest party but the one with the most plausible path to a coalition. Eisenkot is likely to collect more recommendations than Netanyahu, since the Arab parties are expected to back him. Then the clock starts ticking. The chosen candidate has 28 days — and a possible 14-day extension — to negotiate with other parties over cabinet posts, budgets and policies in order to form a government. If he fails, the mandate passes to another candidate for another four weeks. If he fails, too, the Knesset gets a short window to put forward an alternative candidate. If that fails, the country goes to automatic elections. Netanyahu, as caretaker prime minister, has a built-in advantage. If Eisenkot receives the mandate first — and fails — all he needs to do is wait for his time to pass. And if Israel finds itself headed for new elections, Netanyahu will remain caretaker for months. Eisenkot’s options Eisenkot isn’t out of options entirely. Even without forming a government, the opposition could still leverage its parliamentary majority to replace the Knesset speaker and other key positions. That could limit Netanyahu’s ability to govern and even enable the opposition to advance legislation. But Eisenkot, a retired lieutenant general, isn’t on his preferred battlefield. Netanyahu’s coalition remains incredibly loyal, and he doesn’t have to worry in any real way about defections. The same cannot be said for Eisenkot. His diverse coalition is far less ideologically aligned, and even the tiniest step could splinter the bloc and send the country back to elections. For now, the focus is on Herzog, whose role is even more important given the current deadlock. With neither bloc holding a clear majority, he may try to push Netanyahu and Eisenkot to form a unity government. “We must do everything to avoid another round of elections,” Herzog said Wednesday. He called on party leaders to come to consultations with an “open mind.”

articles.title: What we now know about the UK economy in four charts
articles.summary: The Office for Budget Responsibility says higher energy prices will impact everything from prices and living standards to economic growth.
articles.body:
The UK may have no involvement in the US-Iran war, but the country is feeling the full force of the conflict on its economy.

Soaring energy prices are set to dent growth in the short term, push up inflation and leave living standards in a "grim" place, according to the latest official forecast from the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR).

Interest rates are also predicted to rise, making borrowing more expensive, along with government debt repayments.

Chancellor John Healey warned the nation faces "real challenges ahead" as he announced policies that he said would offer "breathing space" for households in the coming months.

Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

"What we face today are global economic storms," he said. "We can't wish them away. We must choose the course we steer through them."

In its first assessment of the UK economy since the Middle East conflict started, the OBR said rising energy prices were the biggest risk to the economy in the near future.

Despite raising its growth forecast for this year, it sharply cut its prediction for next year from 1.6% to 1%.

Growth is then set to rebound in the following years.

When an economy grows, businesses tend to invest more, create more jobs and give pay rises to workers, which leaves people feeling better off on average, though it can take time and not everyone necessarily benefits.

Companies making higher profits also pay more in tax, which can enable the government to spend more on public services. When there is slow economic growth, or the economy shrinks, the opposite can occur.

Inflation can weigh on growth and the OBR has forecast that prices are set to rise at a faster pace as higher energy bills filter through supply chains and to consumers, especially in 2027.

High global oil prices have already hit drivers at the pumps, with petrol priced at almost £1.73 per litre on average, while diesel is near £1.99.

Elevated oil prices over time can lead to prices edging upwards across a host of goods, such as food, as companies pass on the higher expenses they face to consumers.

Goods are typically transported to destinations by lorries and vans, so high fuel prices can have far-reaching consequences.

The OBR now thinks inflation will stay higher for longer than previously forecast, peaking at 3.8% in 2027.

Despite the cost-of-living support announced by the government, economists at Pantheon Macroeconomics said the measures were "small beer given the surge in inflation we expect over the winter".

High inflation paints a bleak picture when it comes to living standards and the OBR has forecast a dip next year as energy bills hit the spending power of households.

Those on lower incomes are set to be hit harder, however, because energy costs eat up a bigger share of their monthly budget and disposable income.

Real household disposable income, a measure of living standards, is forecast to grow from 2027, but not by as much as previously thought.

"It's a pretty grim picture," according to the OBR's David Miles, who says there has been "virtually no growth" for individuals since before the Covid pandemic.

"It's been a dismal period in British economic history."

What the Budget offers for under 25s - and what it leaves out

Inflation is expected to average 3.4% next year, before falling to the Bank of England's 2% target towards the end of the decade.

The Bank is widely expected to raise interest rates next week due to higher inflation in recent months. Rates are currently at 3.75%, but the OBR now forecasts they could rise to as high as 4.5% in the coming years.

It had previously forecast two interest rate cuts this year.

Higher rates makes borrowing money more expensive but can boost returns on savings.

Inflation also raises the cost of borrowing for the government, with spending on debt interest set to rise.

Such repayments are also predicted to increase the overall amount the government borrows, which is set to increase every year by more than had been previously forecast by the OBR.

Higher spending on welfare and pensions due to inflation is also expected to increase borrowing, though it is forecast to fall as a share of the economy over the next five years.

However, forecasts are only a best guess at what might happen in the future. Given the way the conflict in the Middle East has upended previous predictions, the future of the war could alter inflation expectations.

US President Donald Trump has suggested the war will end after the mid-term elections next month.

The OBR admitted there remained "significant uncertainty" around its predictions due to the changing situation in the Middle East.

articles.title: 'Never-ending' cruise grinds to devastating end, stranding over 200 passengers abroad
articles.summary: Retirees aboard the Villa Vie Odyssey cruise ship say they were repeatedly asked for more fuel money before the residential cruise ship halted in Cambodia.
articles.body: A dream cruise around the world has come to an abrupt halt after two years at sea, reportedly leaving passengers scrambling to find somewhere to stay in Cambodia. The Villa Vie Odyssey, a residential cruise ship that promised passengers the chance to make the ocean their permanent home, suspended its voyage Tuesday after its operator said soaring fuel costs had made it too expensive to continue. CRUISE VACATION COMES TO CRASHING HALT AS SHIP SLAMS INTO 2 CARGO VESSELS The ship was carrying 203 passengers, most of them Americans, and 156 crew members when it arrived in the Cambodian port city of Sihanoukville, according to The Associated Press. Passengers said they were given just seven hours' notice to leave the vessel Tuesday and had to make their own arrangements, despite the company's claims that it was helping residents find temporary accommodations. In a statement, Villa Vie Residences, which is headquartered in Florida, announced that it had been "unable to continue carrying the resulting operating losses." The company said monthly fuel expenses per cabin had climbed from roughly $1,800 to as much as $8,000 in parts of Asia. ANGRY CRUISE PASSENGERS SAY FRUSTRATING ISSUE SHOULD HAVE BEEN DISCLOSED BEFORE BOOKING "Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution," the company said, according to the AP. "Our focus now is on supporting residents, crew, and employees." The company added, "The company is working with residents to coordinate disembarkation and identify temporary living arrangements." The ship first set sail from Belfast, Northern Ireland, in October 2024, on what was supposed to be a 3 1/2-year journey around the world. For some passengers, the ship was supposed to be their permanent home long after the initial voyage ended. MAJOR CRUISE LINE HIKES ITS POPULAR PACKAGE PRICES IN MOVE THAT COULD HIT VACATION BUDGETS Fox Business reported in May 2024 that Villa Vie Residences was offering lifetime access to its Odyssey cruise ship through its "Endless Horizons" program for a one-time payment of $299,999 for a single-occupancy cabin or $499,999 for double occupancy. At the time, the experience was billed as a budget-conscious alternative to traditional retirement. "Because it was a startup company, I believe that it was a risk." The company marketed the program to retirees concerned about inflation, rising living expenses and the possibility of outliving their savings. CEO Mikael Petterson similarly promoted the experience as a way for retirees to live on a fixed budget without worrying about ongoing expenses. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "For less than the price of an average home, you can secure a lifetime of experiences," Petterson said at the time. Speaking to AP, passengers expressed disappointment over the abrupt end to their voyage. Paul and Lynn Montoya, a retired couple from Wyoming who boarded the ship 17 months ago, said they purchased a cabin with plans to spend years traveling the world — but were repeatedly asked to contribute more money for fuel. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "We were tired of every two to four weeks being asked for money for fuel, money for everything," Lynn Montoya said. "We had hopes, but they just kept sinking further and further into the hole," the AP reported. California sisters Carol Larson, 69, and Crystal Lavering, 72, also said they were heartbroken after spending 18 months aboard the ship. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Larson, who paid $120,000 for her cabin, said she hoped residents could buy the ship and keep the cruise going. Despite the setback, she told the AP she had no regrets about her investment. "Because it was a startup company, I believe that it was a risk," said Larson. "From the very first day, I said to myself that if it lasts a year, I can walk away and feel like I got my money's worth. … I still feel that way." articles.title: UN votes to condemn embargo of Cuba despite US lobbying push
articles.summary: US points to increase in abstentions in General Assembly as evidence that push to isolate Cuba is slowly succeeding.
articles.body:
The United Nations General Assembly has again voted in favour of a resolution condemning the United States’s economic embargo of Cuba despite a push by US officials to peel off support.

The resolution passed on Wednesday with 130 countries in favour and 17 opposed, including the US and Israel. Another 25 countries abstained, including countries such as Germany and Italy, that had previously voted in favour. The General Assembly has voted to condemn the embargo annually for more than three decades.

Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez said in a social media post after the vote that the US was “once again isolated in its attempt to continue strangling the Cuban people”.

“Neither its most insane pretexts nor its pressures nor media circus will prevail over the force of facts and truth,” he added.

The US embargo on Cuba, part of an effort to isolate the country and squeeze its economy that has lasted more than six decades, has been widely condemned on the world stage and linked to worsening hardship on the island.

US President Donald Trump’s administration has implemented a series of additional economic restrictions , including an energy blockade , to further tighten the screws.

That economic campaign has also been accompanied by a US diplomatic push to further isolate Havana, an effort that US officials said is apparent in the uptick in countries that abstained during Wednesday’s vote. Cuban officials accused the US of threatening countries with tariffs, visa restrictions and other penalties if they voted to condemn the embargo.

“I’m satisfied that so many countries now, including major economies like Korea, like Germany and others have shifted their position,” US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz told reporters after the vote.

“Diplomacy takes time, but now that we’ve had a tripling of countries that have shifted, we expect that to only continue to grow,” he added.

Tensions between US and Cuban officials exploded on Tuesday during a General Assembly debate with both yelling at the other and engaging in an apparent shoving match.

Waltz said on Wednesday that Richard Tur de la Concepcion, a first secretary at Cuba’s UN mission, would be expelled from the country for “assaulting an American diplomat”.

Al Jazeera has reached out to the US and Cuban missions for comment but has not received a response.

images.caption: United Nations member states voted to end the economic commercial and financial embargo imposed by the US on Cuba in the General Assembly in New York [File: Peter Foley/EPA]

articles.title: New look at texts, phone data leads to murder charge in disappearance of ‘The People’s Court’ co-participant
articles.summary: A fresh look at cellphone data and text messages led to the arrest of a Florida man accused of murdering his ex-fiancée within hours of taping an episode for “The People’s Court” in 2011, court documents unsealed Tuesday revealed.
articles.body: A fresh look at cellphone data and text messages led to the arrest of a Florida man accused of murdering his ex-fiancée within hours of taping an episode for “The People’s Court” in 2011, court documents unsealed Tuesday revealed. Dale Smith Jr., a 55-year-old Orlando resident, was taken into custody Oct. 14 and charged with second-degree murder in the death of Michelle Parker, whose body has never been found, police said. Smith was 40 and Parker 33 when she was last seen alive on Nov. 17, 2011, the day the episode was taped. The two shared custody of twins at the time. That afternoon, at about 2 p.m., Parker and Smith appeared for a taping of “The People’s Court” to settle a dispute over a $5,000 engagement ring she allegedly threw off a balcony. The judge ruled “that both parties were responsible for the ring and ordered they split the $5,000.00 damage,” according to an arrest warrant affidavit. Smith told investigators that, after the taping of the show, Parker dropped the children off at his home and left about 10 minutes later, police said. But surveillance cameras appeared to show that “the victim’s Hummer was at the suspect’s residence for at least one hour,” according to the affidavit. Surveillance cameras showed Parker arriving at Smith’s building at about 3:18 p.m., according to the affidavit. At about 4:18 p.m. “victim and suspect phones leaves suspect’s home,” the document said. By 4:32 p.m., the “victim’s and suspect’s phones continue moving west” the affidavit said, a route that conflicted with Parker’s plans. “The victim was to travel north to pick up her oldest son who was waiting for her,” it said. Parker’s brother, Dustin Erickson, also texted her that afternoon asking where she was. Her phone replied, “Waterford,” according to the affidavit. “Waterford” is the common local name for the Waterford Lakes Town Center shopping mall, about 12 miles northeast of Smith’s home. “The victim’s cell phone never travels east or north towards the Waterford Lakes shopping center,” the affidavit said. “According to Dustin Erickson, the victim had no reason to deceive Dustin as to her location.” Smith has previously said he had no idea where Parker went after dropping off the children. He told investigators he thought she was “laying low” after the “People’s Court” episode aired, the affidavit said. “He wanted the victim to come home safe for their kids. However, according to his phone records, he never called or messaged her ever again after November 17, 2011,” the document said. Police said Smith has a history of domestic violence. Detectives interviewed Jill Van Mechelen, another of his ex-fiancées, whom he knew before he met Parker. “According to Jill Van Mechelen, the suspect would manually choke (strangle) her during these episodes of domestic physical violence,” the affidavit said. “The suspect also made threats to kill Jill Van Mechelen and her father. Jill Van Mechelen reported that the suspect told her on multiple occasions that he would kill her and/or her father and make them disappear.” Smith’s attorney declined comment on Wednesday, citing a court gag order.

articles.title: Hayden Panettiere’s death is ruled accidental, and police investigation is closed
articles.summary: Panettiere, 36, died of the toxic effects of multiple drugs, including fentanyl, the coroner determined.
articles.body: Actor Hayden Panettiere’s death has been ruled an accident, and the case is now closed, police in South Carolina announced Wednesday. “Based on the Medical Examiner’s determination and the findings of the investigation, Hayden Panettiere’s death has been ruled accidental,” Greenville police said, noting the investigation has concluded. Panettiere, 36, the actor who starred in the shows “Heroes” and “Nashville,” was found unresponsive Aug. 16 in a South Carolina apartment complex where she was staying. Last month, the Greenville County Coroner’s Office ruled her death an accident caused by the toxic effects of multiple drugs: fentanyl, 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol and quetiapine. The coroner said there were no signs of trauma that would have contributed to her death. Police also have said no signs of foul play were found during the initial response and investigation. Panettiere, who had publicly discussed her struggle with addiction, had been in rehab just weeks before, according to the coroner’s report. Panettiere’s on-again, off-again boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, was at the apartment complex at the time of her death. He showed police a “bag of medication” he said she was taking at the time, according to the police report. After the coroner’s report was issued, Panettiere’s mother, Lesley Vogel, called her daughter a “fighter” who was “transparent with her addictions and her numerous rehab attempts show her resolve to live a healthy life.” Vogel also said at the time that she had “never heard Hayden speak of fentanyl.” Panettiere entered Hollywood as a child actor and later carved her own path, starring in the films “Remember the Titans,” “Ice Princess” and “Bring It On: All or Nothing.” In her memoir, she detailed how her life began to spiral after she had a daughter with Ukrainian heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko in 2014. She began drinking heavily to cope with postpartum depression and Klitschko’s distance, she wrote in the book. She checked into rehab and gave Klitschko custody of their child in 2018. In the book, she also discussed grappling with pain and grief after her brother, Jansen Panettiere, died in 2023 from an undiagnosed heart condition.

articles.title: Costa Rica’s mega-prison receives first inmates
articles.summary: President Laura Fernandez inaugurated the $35m mega-prison built to house up to 5,100 inmates near San Jose.
articles.body:
A newly opened maximum-security mega-prison in Costa Rica has received its first batch of inmates. The prison was built with the help of the Salvadoran government on the outskirts of the capital, San Jose, the country’s Justice Ministry announced.

The Costa Rican Justice Ministry shared images on Tuesday of 123 inmates dressed in orange, seated with their heads shaved and bowed and their hands behind their necks.

“Costa Rica is writing a new chapter in its penitentiary history,” Justice Minister Gabriel Aguilar said in a statement.

The new prison is called the High-Containment Center Against Organized Crime (CACCO) and constitutes a symbol of a new “tough on crime” approach championed by President Laura Fernandez ’s administration. It has a capacity for 5,100 inmates.

The CACCO was built with the help of the Salvadoran government on the outskirts of Costa Rica’s capital, San Jose, at a cost of $35m. Fernandez inaugurated it on October 15.

“CACCO is a monument to national security, a forceful response to organized crime, and a guarantee that the state will exercise its authority without hesitation,” the statement added.

The new facility has a capacity equivalent to 20 percent of the country’s prison population and “will also help reduce overcrowding in the prison system”, according to Aguilar.

Costa Rica , long regarded as one of the safest countries in Latin America, has in recent years experienced a sharp rise in violence linked to drug trafficking and organised crime. It witnessed a record-setting 905 homicides in 2023, followed by 876 in 2024 and 873 in 2025.

Authorities attribute most killings to disputes between criminal groups over drug trafficking routes and markets.

Right-wing leaders in other Latin American countries have also sought to replicate the mega-prison model.

articles.title: High-speed train crash kills at least 68 people in Spain
articles.summary: The crash, between a moving train and another that was stopped further up the track, was caused by an "inexplicable" error, the transport minister said.
articles.body:
A high-speed train crash has killed at least 68 people and injured dozens more in central Spain.

It occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville barrelled into another train - which was stationary on the tracks - on Wednesday morning. The force saw several carriages fall down an embankment.

The transport minister said a computer failure followed by human error caused the collision, which is one of the worst in Europe's modern history, and Spain's deadliest train disaster in 13 years.

Survivors described harrowing scenes of passengers being thrown into the air, trapped in the wreckage and smashing windows to get out.

The collision happened just after 09:00 (08:00 GMT) around 140km (100 miles) south of Madrid.

The stationary train, run by private rail operator Iryo, had 147 passengers on board, and had stopped on the tracks because of a computer failure, Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente said.

He explained that when there is a system failure, a 24-hour control centre in Madrid takes over, but it had made an "inexplicable" decision to instruct the trains to move again, without any speed restrictions.

Iryo said its train was "struck from behind" by another train, run by Spain's state-owned railway company, Renfe, which was carrying 397 passengers.

The force of the crash was "brutal", said 62-year-old passenger Salvador Arriza who was sitting in the Renfe-operated train.

Passengers started breaking the windows to get out, he told Reuters, adding that "some people couldn't move because they were trapped amongst the seats."

One of the carriages caught fire, and passengers described devastating scenes of trapped people crying and bleeding, with some buried under debris.

Pictures show that a long piece of railway track had speared through one of the carriages.

Tangui Binier, 22, was on the Iryo train and told the BBC that "suitcases started flying and people were screaming" when the train finally came to a halt.

There was a lot of smoke and confusion, he said, and described seeing the train "completely flipped over" when he stepped outside.

"It was hard to witness", Binier said, adding that his father carried a girl who had a broken hip out of the wreckage.

He also described seeing dead bodies and missing limbs: "I don't know if I'll ever recover."

Spanish journalist Antonio Jiménez Barca, who works for El Pais newspaper, was walking to the Renfe train's cafeteria when the crash happened.

"I felt like I was being pushed from behind, like I was being thrown to the ground," he described.

"I hit my head horribly... I was covered in blood. There were people on top of me. One person had an injured arm, and another had a head injury."

Another passenger, 46-year-old Sebastián Herrero, told El Mundo newspaper that he saw "many people with broken noses, broken arms."

"It was a terrible, terrible impact," he said, adding that he was "in the air for about four or five seconds," which felt like a lifetime.

Many of the passengers said they were in shock, and one sobbed during an interview with a local television station as he described a woman dying in his arms.

"She was very cold and she was all alone," he said, to which the show's presenter also started to cry.

Dozens of ambulances rushed to the scene, and a helicopter evacuated those with the most serious injuries.

Spain's Civil Guard said it would need DNA samples from relatives to identify some victims.

"The whole of Spain is grieving", Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said during a visit to the crash site. "Lives have been shattered, families have been torn apart, the pain is immense."

Spain was already reeling from a high-speed rail disaster near Córdoba in January that killed 46 people. It happened on the same rail line, but much further south.

Wednesday's crash is the worst the country has seen since 2013, when when 80 people died on the outskirts of Santiago de Compostela in north-west Spain.

"Spain has the right to know what is happening with its infrastructure," said Alberto Núñez Feijóo, leader of the the main opposition People's Party.

Spanish trade union CSIF has demanded the transport minister resign, accusing him of "scapegoating" a traffic manager, by blaming human error in the control room, instead of "taking responsibility".

Sánchez and other Spanish politicians cancelled all public engagements on Wednesday, including campaigning for next month's parliamentary elections.

The prime minister said it was "unacceptable" for Spain to have two serious train crashes in one year, and vowed to "get to the bottom of this" and determine if there was any negligence.

"If there have been failures in the security system, they will be addressed with the utmost firmness."

articles.title: Vance sends letter to Iran hard-liner in bid to revive peace talks as Trump threatens strikes: Report
articles.summary: US vice president JD Vance has opened a direct channel to one of Iran’s most powerful hard-liners in an attempt to revive peace negotiations according to
articles.body: US vice president JD Vance has opened a direct channel to one of Iran’s most powerful hard-liners in an attempt to revive peace negotiations according to a report by the Wall Street Journal. This developments comes even as US president Donald Trump threatens to resume military strikes in the coming weeks.Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council and a former commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), in an outreach intended to test whether Washington and Tehran can agree on a framework for negotiations. The letter was sent at Trump’s direction, according to one person familiar with the matter cited by WSJ, and the president is aware of the initiative.Separately, Trump has denied directing Vance to initiate peace negotiations with Iran, saying the vice president’s contact concerned medical supplies. “Iran needs help with medical supplies. Basically, it’s getting supplies in to help people that are not well,” Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews when asked whether he had instructed Vance to begin peace talks.The effort comes as Trump weighs a short, intense new attack on Iran after next week’s US midterm elections. Vance is seeking to establish whether diplomacy can avert another round of fighting, though the discussions have yet to produce a detailed peace proposal. Rezaei said last week that Iran would not negotiate with Washington until its core demands were met.The outreach marks a delicate balancing act for Vance, who has publicly backed the war but privately expressed reservations about prolonging it. Before Trump launched “Operation Epic Fury” in February, Vance argued for more robust diplomacy. Trump later appointed him lead negotiator, and the vice president travelled abroad twice to meet Iranian counterparts in pursuit of an agreement to end the conflict.A memorandum of understanding reached in June collapsed just two weeks after it was signed, amid competing interpretations of how shipping through the Strait of Hormuz would be restored. Subsequent negotiations, mediated by Qatar and Pakistan, have failed to break the deadlock. Washington wants Iran to make nuclear concessions upfront, while Tehran is demanding immediate economic relief.Rezaei’s emergence as a key interlocutor could also reshape the diplomatic process, potentially sidelining figures such as Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. A veteran of Iran’s 1980s war with Iraq who led the IRGC for years, Rezaei has become an influential voice as the threat of renewed US attacks grows.Earlier this month, he warned that Iran could target the United Arab Emirates, as well as data centres and internet cables across the region. On Sunday, he met security chiefs from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey in Tehran in a rare engagement at that level, as regional powers sought to contain the conflict.Trump, meanwhile, has alternated between pursuing a diplomatic settlement and threatening to bomb Iran into submission, with dismantling its nuclear programme a central national-security priority of his second term. He said last week that Washington was not negotiating with Tehran and suggested military action was imminent. During a campaign stop on Tuesday, he accused Iran of dragging out efforts to reach a deal and warned that waiting until after the election would not help it.Republicans face the prospect of losing seats in the House and Senate in the midterms, with voters citing the war and rising fuel prices among their concerns. Vance, an early contender for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, is therefore navigating a conflict that carries both foreign-policy and domestic political risks.Trump has said the war will end only when he decides it should.
